input: In this study, dimethyl ether was produced from carbon dioxide and hydrogen over a copper-zinc oxide catalyst, and two different catalyst forms, namely a structured form and a conventional pellet form, were compared with one another under a single set of test conditions. The tests were carried out at 280 °C and 40 bar, with a feed ratio H2/CO2 = 3 and one feed composition throughout. The space-time yield, which is defined as the mass of product obtained per unit catalyst volume per hour (kg L-1 h-1), was used as the principal measure of performance. The structured catalyst achieved a space-time yield of 0.9 kg L-1 h-1, together with a pressure drop of only 0.1 bar and an activity loss of 5% after 100 h on stream. In contrast, the pellet catalyst gave a considerably lower space-time yield of 0.47 kg L-1 h-1, a much higher pressure drop of 1.28 bar, and a substantially larger activity loss of 18% after 100 h. Overall, the results show that the structured form outperforms the pellet form on all three of the measures reported here. It should be noted, however, that the comparison is based on a single feed composition, that no sulfur-bearing feed was tested, and that yield and pressure drop are seldom reported for the same catalyst charge, which makes wider comparisons with the existing literature rather difficult.
target: Dimethyl ether was prepared from carbon dioxide and hydrogen over a copper-zinc oxide catalyst in two forms, a structured form and a pellet form, and the two forms were compared under one set of test conditions at one feed composition. The test conditions were a temperature of 280 °C and a pressure of 40 bar, with a feed ratio H2/CO2 = 3. Space-time yield is the mass of product per unit catalyst volume per hour (kg L-1 h-1), and the comparison rests on the space-time yield, the pressure drop and the activity loss measured over the test duration. The structured catalyst gave a space-time yield of 0.9 kg L-1 h-1, a pressure drop of 0.1 bar and an activity loss of 5% after 100 h. The pellet catalyst gave a space-time yield of 0.47 kg L-1 h-1, a pressure drop of 1.28 bar and an activity loss of 18% after 100 h. At the stated conditions the structured form has the higher space-time yield, the lower pressure drop and the smaller activity loss, and the three measures rank the two forms in the same order. Activity loss is stated at the end of the stated duration for both forms, so the stability comparison is drawn at a common time on stream. The comparison is limited to the one feed composition tested and to the stated conditions. No sulfur-bearing feed was tested, and yield and pressure drop are seldom reported for the same catalyst charge, which limits the comparison that can be drawn with other catalysts.
